title: Chapter 204: Don't Take the Elevator
html:
The black phone’s hint for the Tape Ghost’s affection mission had read: Honey, black, white, and red—which color do you prefer?

Since then, those three colors had caught Chen Ge’s attention. Wang Xin’s adoptive mother favored black and white, while the woman from the elevator had worn red heels. In his eyes, both deserved suspicion.

Studying Wang Xin’s mother more closely, Chen Ge realized that everything about her—from her appearance to the way she carried herself—made her seem younger than her age. She was still beautiful; in her youth, she must have been striking.

Patient No. 2 is terrified of growing old…Chen Ge grew warier. His gaze dropped to the teacup in her hand, and he was grateful he had not touched his own.

“Doctor Chen.” She stepped closer, apparently noticing the change in him. “Did my story frighten you?”

“A little.” Chen Ge played along. “Would you mind telling me which apartment was haunted?”

“Room 3133 on the thirteenth floor. The police said the white figure ran inside, but the owner wasn’t even home. I heard she moved away soon afterward, and the incident was forgotten. No one was hurt, and nothing was stolen, so there was little we tenants could do.”

“Perhaps she never moved away,” Chen Ge murmured.

“What did you say?”

“Nothing. I was only wondering why her room number contains so many threes.” Since leaving the Third Sick Hall, Chen Ge had noticed the number appearing with unsettling frequency. Even the countdown for summoning the mirror ghost had begun at three.

“3133 means Building Three, thirteenth floor, Room Three,” she explained.

“Security told me most of the thirteenth-floor tenants have already moved out. Has anything else happened in the past year or two?”

“I don’t think so, though most of us avoid going out at night.” After a moment’s thought, she added, “But I should warn you: when you leave, don’t take the elevator. Several months ago, a drunk man rode it at night. It stopped on the thirteenth floor, and a white figure stepped inside.”

“The elevator should have a camera. Wouldn’t it have recorded everything? Didn’t the landlord explain what happened?” Chen Ge committed every word to memory.

“The man was so frightened that he confronted the landlord the next day. It caused quite a commotion.” Wang Xin’s mother searched her memory. “The landlord retrieved the footage, but no white figure appeared. It showed only the drunk man pressing buttons at random. He rode from the first floor to the top and back down, stopping several times, but the camera never captured anyone entering.”

“The doors opened several times?”

“Briefly each time. Only on the thirteenth floor did they remain open longer than usual. The landlord claimed someone had called the elevator, then changed their mind after seeing the drunk man inside.”

“That explanation sounds forced.”

“It does, but since then, we’ve rarely used the elevator at night.”

Chen Ge nodded. “Do you think I could obtain the footage?”

“The landlord probably kept a copy. I can ask tomorrow morning.”

“Thank you.” As a civilian, Chen Ge had no authority to demand a building’s surveillance footage. He took his leave, but after the door closed, he doubled back. Removing a sheet of paper from his backpack, he folded it several times and wedged it into the doorframe.

She had said she rarely went out at night. If the paper fell before morning, she would become a serious suspect. His trap set, Chen Ge took the stairs to the thirteenth floor.

Only the thirteenth floor lacked sound-activated lighting. The green emergency-exit sign provided the corridor’s sole illumination, its sickly glow making the darkness more oppressive. Ballpoint pen in hand, Chen Ge stepped inside. The floor appeared abandoned, and dust coated every door.

“Room 3133.” Chen Ge found the former home of the disturbed woman. Unlike the other doors, this one was spotless, as though someone still lived inside. His flashlight revealed a fresh sheet of paper taped to it: the owner was offering the apartment for sale or rent at a low price, followed by a phone number.

Someone bought this place after the mad woman left?

The notice looked recently posted. Chen Ge listened outside the apartment, but when no sound came from within, he walked away and dialed the number. It rang for nearly half a minute. Just as he was about to give up, someone answered.

“Hello. I saw the advertisement at Fang Hwa Apartments. The price seems reasonable, and I’m interested.” Chen Ge felt tense. Calling so late might expose his true intentions.

Silence answered him. At last, a woman said, “I’m seriously ill and need money for my medical expenses. That’s why the price is so low. If you truly want to buy it, name a time. We can meet at Xin Kang Apartments in the old part of town.”

“Xin Kang Apartments?”

“My condition could worsen at any time, so I moved closer to the hospital. I’m on the third floor.”

“Okay, I’ll go now.”

“Now?” Her voice rose, turning slightly shrill. “All right. Come now, then.”

After hanging up, Chen Ge’s suspicion deepened. The old district had no major hospital. Why had she lied?

The moment he left Building Three, the weight in the air seemed to lift. He took a taxi to Xin Kang Apartments, hurried to the third floor, and called again. “I’m here. There are three apartments on this floor. Which one is yours?”

“Wait a moment.” The call ended, and the door to his left opened. “Come in. The room is messy, but I haven’t had the energy to clean.”

Chen Ge pushed the door open, and his heart clenched. The woman had neither hair nor eyebrows. Her pallid, featureless face was deeply unsettling.
